subject: Hosted API quote consolidation & sliding-slab concession request
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina@astratech.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@astratech.com
Date: 2027-05-10T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing — usage forecast & ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. We're evaluating consolidating our sandbox and prod traffic into a single committed path (hosted API) and wanted a clear picture of how that would map to commit tiers and per-token pricing.

Attached is our 6‑month forecast (baseline + upside). High level: we expect an average of ~18B tokens/month with seasonal spikes to ~26B. Our procurement lead wants a predictable blended unit price for budgeting. Can you share what committed tiers you recommend and any flexibility on the published rate card for a 12‑month commit?

Specific asks:
- A sliding-slab example that consolidates sandbox + prod (single invoice)
- Any floor/ceiling protections if we miss the commit in Q1
- A draft concessions matrix we can take to internal finance

Attachment: [astratech_forecast_may2027.csv (CSV, 34KB)]

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships
AstraTech
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina@astratech.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — usage forecast & ask

Hi Nina — thanks for the forecast and for laying out the ask clearly. I've looped in Karthik (pricing lead) and Vanessa (AE) so we can move quickly.

High-level initial read: 18B sustained with spikes to 26B is in the band where a committed tier materially reduces per-token cost versus on-list hosted rates. Rather than a single flat rate, we recommend a sliding-slab commit (monthly consumption buckets that map to blended price) — this preserves predictability while allowing you to benefit from upside.

What I'm proposing next (attached): priyom_astratech_concession_matrix.xlsx — a 3-tier commit structure: 12M total with quarterly checkpoints. Concessions shown are conditional on: 1) 12‑month committed spend, 2) a minimal ramp schedule (Q1 ≥ 50% of target), 3) standardized data retention & audit terms.

Ask from my side: I will need an internal pricing exception to soften the rate card at the 18B and 22B breakpoints. The proposed deviations are visible in the spreadsheet (column "proposed client price"). Can either Karthik or Vanessa confirm whether I should route this to the Pricing Committee or straight to Finance for approval?

Proposed next steps:
- Internal approval (pricing exception)
- Legal to prepare SOW with the agreed commit and refund/true-up language
- DocuSign-ready copy for signatures

Attachments: [priyom_astratech_concession_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 82KB)]

Thanks — I can jump on a call if helpful.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — usage forecast & ask

Priyom — reviewed the matrix. A few internal notes for the request:

- Baseline vs. upside: We should clearly separate the guaranteed commit (baseline) from the upside slab that triggers better pricing. Finance will expect a conservative baseline. Recommend baseline = 18B/mo equivalent and upside bands at 22B and 26B.
- Shortfall and floor: Any shortfall in the baseline should trigger a true‑up at a pre-agreed fallback rate (not worse than list). We should avoid refundable credits that are open‑ended; limited ramp credits are ok.
- Margins: Proposed concessions at the 18B band are at the edge of our allowable discount for hosted API; to approve we need Rishi's signoff.
- Pricing governance: Because this request changes list rate at two breakpoints, route to Pricing Committee (PRIC-321) and add a note for a capped discount and time‑limited promotion (12 months).

I recommend we ask Rishi to approve a conditional exception: up to 15% off list at 18B, up to 25% at 22B, subject to 12‑month commit and quarterly usage reporting. If legal can accept the true‑up language (I flagged a sample clause), I'm comfortable moving this to Finance for SOW creation.

Can you place this into PRIC-321 and ping Rishi? I can draft the internal approval note.

—Karthik
Director, Pricing Operations
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-12T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: AstraTech conditional hosted API concession

Team — reviewed the concession matrix and Karthik's notes. Approve a conditional pricing exception with the following guardrails: 

1) Commit: 12 months, minimum annualized commitment equivalent to 18B tokens/month.
2) Breakpoints & concessions: up to 15% off list at 18B; up to 23% off list at 22B; any pricing better than these requires CEO approval.
3) Ramp credit: single one‑time ramp credit equal to 5% of first quarter estimated spend; fully earned if Q1 usage ≥ 50% of target, clawback if below target per SOW.
4) True‑up: shortfalls billed at the published fallback rate; overages billed at the contracted per-token increment.
5) Reporting: quarterly usage export and access to token-level metering for audit.
6) Duration of exception: 12 months from signature — renewal requires fresh review.

Please route to Legal to draft SOW and to Finance to prepare the invoice schedule. Vanessa — prioritize getting the vendor procurement language on data retention in the SOW. Priyom — once Legal confirms the SOW language, prepare the DocuSign packet and propose signature timeline.

I've attached a sample terms template (signed_terms_template_v2.docx) with the approved clause language. Make sure the HubSpot deal AST-2027-045 reflects the approved concession and update PRIC-321 with the disposition.

Rishi
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
